title: Spine X-ray for scoliosis
what: An X-ray of the spine while standing, often full length. From it, the doctor measures the angle of the curve.
why: For uneven posture, shoulders or shoulder blades at different heights, possible scoliosis, or to check treatment.
duration: usually 10 to 15 minutes in the room; the report the same or the next day
tell_doctor: If you are or might be pregnant
If you wear a brace. Ask whether the X-ray is taken with it or without it
Past spine X-rays and their dates

prepare.title: Prep
prepare.text: None needed. You can eat and drink.

prepare.title: Clothing
prepare.text: Take off anything with metal: clasps, zippers, an underwire bra, necklaces. Sometimes a disposable gown is given.

bring: Past spine X-rays. Without them, it is hard to compare the angle
steps: You undress down to your underwear
You stand with your back or side to the machine, feet level
Your arms rest at your sides or on a support
Stand straight and hold your breath for a couple of seconds
Sometimes images are taken while bending to the sides
feel: You just need to stand straight. It is easy
after: You can go about your day right away
Take the report with the curve angle to an orthopedic or spine specialist

faq.q: How often can a scoliosis X-ray be done?
faq.a: As often as your doctor orders. Usually no more than once every 6 to 12 months, unless there is a special reason.

faq.q: Why is a child imaged standing, not lying down?
faq.a: Lying down, the curve gets smaller. Standing shows the true angle.

reminders.text: Spine X-ray soon. Wear underwear with no metal and bring past X-rays.
